title: The Tribute
text: “However—!”
“Father!”
Fiancée raised her voice loudly, cutting Trash off.

“Mother has already voiced her concerns, but let me say this too. Please calm yourself. You mustn’t let your hatred for Siltvelt cloud your judgment. Shield Hero-sama is not the one who took what was precious to you, Father.”
Fiancée had come to understand Father’s true character over these past few days, I say, so her warning came from a place of genuine conviction that the problem lay entirely with Trash.

“The delay in my return, and the false rumor that reached your ears claiming I’d been kidnapped by Shield Hero-sama—all of it was a conspiracy orchestrated by those in the Three Heroes Church, our nation’s own religion. It was the very knights who accompanied me who raised swords and cast spells against me. Did you know that?”

“And on top of that, they dared to declare that I, acting under Mother’s orders, had no need to reconcile with Shield Hero-sama. These are people who defied a royal command. You mustn’t let yourself be swayed by the schemes of those who defied Mother’s orders.”

Trash, faced with his beloved daughter’s reproach, couldn’t quite bring himself to show open anger, nor could he simply accept her words. That was the sort of expression he wore, indeed. Normally this would have been the point where the conversation stalled into a standoff, with Trash deflecting the subject until it dissolved into vagueness.
“What happened to the knights of the castle, then?!”
“That is… they were single-mindedly bent on killing me, so regrettably, I had them dealt with.”
“Melty, there’s no way you could have raised a hand against our nation’s own knights. Surely—”

Since it wouldn’t do to say that Itsuki had wiped them all out, Fiancée had reported to Trash that she’d executed them herself. Trash, seizing what he clearly thought was a golden opportunity, opened his mouth to speak. That was when Rafumi, disguised as Ren, swept in with a dramatic flourish of her cloak and stepped between Fiancée and Trash… wrapping her cloak around herself like some kind of Filolial Cross Trash had once pulled off in another loop, and flashing a bold, fearless grin.

“This ugly little family squabble is not something to be had here and now. What good does it do to speculate on the truth without actual facts? As Sword Hero, I find it unbecoming to keep watching this shameless, misdirected grudge play out before me any further.”
Trash glared daggers at Ren as if to say don’t butt in, clearly irritated, but given that he was supposedly cooperating with the man, he seemed torn over whether to push back hard.

“Listen, King. Naofumi has heard about your circumstances here in the kingdom, and it’s been weighing on his heart, I say. That’s precisely why, in between managing his various projects in the country, he’s been searching for a way to reconcile with you.”
“Shield… with me?”
Trash let out a sharp, scoffing laugh through his nose. His whole demeanor screamed that reconciliation was about as likely as the heavens falling to earth.
“As part of that effort, along with delivering Princess Melty safely home, he’s brought along a tribute for you… he asks that you accept it and give it some thought.”
With that, Rafumi—still disguised as Ren—brought forward a figure seated in a wheelchair, draped heavily in a robe, and set them down in front of Trash.
“I don’t care what he’s brought, Shield thinking he can just—”
Just as Trash was about to declare that no matter what was presented, reconciliation was absolutely out of the question, Rafumi stripped the robe from the person in the wheelchair.
“Ah…”

What appeared there was none other than Tiger Girl. And wouldn’t you know it, it had been Rafumi’s own suggestion to rush Tiger Girl—who’d been in Zeltoble—into treatment and send her over. Along the way, her skin had already been healed thanks to the medicinal effects of a Hero’s power. She was nearly well enough to stand on her own, though apparently the wheelchair was still more effective for now. I’d left the details to Rafumi with an “I’ll leave the rest to you,” and honestly, I was startled at how quickly she’d brought her here.
“Wh… wh… what—?!”
The rage that had twisted Trash’s face dissolved instantly into pure shock at the sight. As for Tiger Girl, she turned toward Trash and tilted her head, over and over, in confusion.
“…Big Brother… no, that’s not right, is it? Though your presence feels remarkably similar.”
Trash pointed at Tiger Girl, utterly at a loss, then turned to Rafumi as if demanding an explanation.

“Even Naofumi hasn’t fully grasped the circumstances himself, but word reached him that in Zeltoble there was a slave who bore a striking resemblance to your late sister. Using every means available within the kingdom, he managed to acquire her… and the proposal is that this tribute might serve as a path toward reconciliation.”
“Guh… guhhhhhhhh!”
Trash clenched his fists tight, trembling, clearly at a total loss as to what emotion he should even be feeling—rage or tears.

“Of course… Naofumi’s heart ached at the thought of using her as some kind of tool. But then, how else could this be conveyed to you? Even I didn’t think it was a bad idea, which is why I delivered her here myself. Understand—this is, first and foremost, an act of goodwill.”
Fiancée, meanwhile, looked back and forth between Trash and Tiger Girl, clearly bewildered.
“F-Father? Um…”
Trash’s face was cycling through so many wildly different expressions it was almost comical.

“No answer is required right away. Take whatever time you need to sort out your feelings. But regarding this arrangement, please understand it was born of conspiracy and misunderstanding, and act accordingly. Now then, allow me to rest a while. I’ll be staying at the castle for some time, so call if anything comes up.”
“Beloved pet little sister, Lolita, the Dark Holy Hero shall seek a moment’s peace before the next battle—blind young lady, White Tiger, farewell~”
And so, with Trash, Tiger Girl, Fiancée, and Filo-tan left behind, Rafumi and Ren’s companions departed the scene.
After Rafumi and the others had left, Trash’s trembling, clenched fists slowly relaxed as he approached Tiger Girl with gentle steps.
“Um… what exactly should I do?”
“It’s all right… you don’t need to worry about a thing. Did those people do something cruel to you?”

“No… someone appeared out of nowhere claiming to want me, wrapped in an almost maddening kind of love… and someone with an incredibly sweet scent and a divine presence healed my illness and brought me here… That said, if there’s anything I can do, I’ll do it. Surely that’s why I was brought here.”
At Tiger Girl’s answer, Trash’s face fell into sorrow, and then—to a degree that even startled Fiancée—softened into an expression of tenderness as he took her hand and stroked it gently.
“Melty.”
“Yes.”
Fiancée, who had been silently watching Trash’s complete transformation from a man consumed by hatred, answered him.
“…Issue a proclamation revoking the bounty on Shield.”
“Y-yes, sir!”
“Ah, Mel-chan, wait up—!”
Fiancée, wearing a faint look of bewilderment at Trash’s answer, immediately left the throne room together with Filo-tan. What remained were Trash and Tiger Girl.
“Well then, shall we move somewhere you can rest properly? Is there… anything you’d like to eat? I’d be delighted if you told me all sorts of things later.”
“Y-yes…”

With that, Trash personally pushed the wheelchair carrying Tiger Girl and escorted her to her room. Just to be safe, it would probably be wise to keep watch in stealth mode for a while. The Three Heroes Church hadn’t been dealt with yet. Within Melromarc Castle, before the Queen’s return, there was no telling when some blade might turn against Tiger Girl.
“My King! That woman is—?!”

Not just the soldiers, but the knights and ministers throughout the hall raised their voices, glaring at Tiger Girl with obvious resentment. But Trash silenced them all with a sharp, intimidating glare.
“I will not allow a single soul to harm this child! This is absolute!”
“Y-yes, sir!”

Everyone snapped to attention at Trash’s command, though their postures still carried the air of people scheming to strike the moment an opening appeared. Of course, Trash was not so blind as to miss that undercurrent. His expression suggested he was turning over all manner of thoughts in his mind. Since Rafumi had said she’d look after Tiger Girl’s wellbeing, there was no need for me to linger here any longer. And so, I retraced my steps and slipped out of the castle.
